questions.q: What does 'availability' measure in a distributed system?
options: The number of servers a system has
The fraction of time a system is usable out of the time it's supposed to be running
How fast a single request completes
How many requests a system can process per second
questions.explain: Availability is about uptime versus intended runtime, usually expressed as a percentage such as 99.9%.

questions.q: Roughly how much allowed downtime per year does going from 99.9% to 99.99% availability remove?
options: It removes almost all downtime, cutting it by about a factor of ten
It has no real effect on allowed downtime
It doubles allowed downtime
It only matters for systems with a global audience
questions.explain: Each additional nine cuts allowed downtime by roughly a factor of ten — 99.9% allows about 8.76 hours a year, while 99.99% allows about 52.6 minutes.

questions.q: What is the primary mechanism distributed systems use to raise availability?
options: Writing more efficient application code
Redundancy paired with automatic failover
Increasing the clock speed of the main server
Reducing the number of users allowed to connect
questions.explain: Running more than one copy of a critical component (redundancy) and automatically switching traffic to a surviving copy when one fails (failover) is the main lever for availability.

questions.q: A system has ten redundant web servers, but all traffic passes through exactly one load balancer. What is the load balancer in this scenario?
options: A failover mechanism
An SLA
A single point of failure
A reliability metric
questions.explain: Even with redundant web servers behind it, a single unreplicated load balancer is a single point of failure — if it fails, the whole system becomes unreachable.

questions.q: How does availability differ from reliability?
options: They are two names for exactly the same measurement
Availability asks if the system is usable right now; reliability asks if it keeps working correctly over time, including through failures
Reliability only applies to databases, availability only applies to web servers
Availability is measured in dollars, reliability is measured in nines
questions.explain: Availability is a snapshot of current usability, while reliability is about consistent correct behavior over time — a system can be available right now yet still have a poor reliability track record.
